identity.name: Mamata Machinery
identity.industry: Packaging Machinery (plastic bag/pouch-making + flexible-packaging/converting + co-extrusion blown film) · Capital Goods

summary.oneLiner: India's leading converting-machinery manufacturer and among the top five globally, Mamata Machinery is a total solutions partner in flexible packaging with capabilities spanning co-extrusion, converting and packaging.
summary.business: Mamata Machinery designs and manufactures machinery for the flexible packaging industry, with an installed base of over 5,400 machines operating across more than 80 countries. Backed by expertise in polymer processing, plastic rheology, converting, filling and sealing systems, it serves both brand owners and convertors through a single technology platform. Over more than 35 years it has grown from a single-product manufacturer into a complete provider of flexible packaging machinery present across the entire value chain, from co-extrusion to converting to packaging.

currentContext.expansion: Mamata's expansion is footprint- and technology-led rather than a large plant build-out. The operating model deliberately combines in-house capabilities across design, software development, engineering, electrical integration, testing and critical operations with a robust network of specialised manufacturing partners, an approach the Company says enhances scalability and operational agility while allowing efficient capital deployment. Historically the footprint was built by establishing Mamata Enterprises Inc. (MEI), a wholly owned US subsidiary, setting up a facility in Florida, USA to support MEI's packaging machine initiatives and North American service capability, and later shifting packaging machine manufacturing from the United States to India to improve operational integration, scalability and supply chain efficiency; the Company also acquired full ownership of its extrusion joint venture (originally a 50:50 JV with Brampton Engineering Inc., Canada) along with technology transfer rights. Current expansion is geographic and product-led: a branch office set up in the CIS and Russia region alongside a hundred-year-old local distributor, channel partners in place in South-East Asia, a partnership with Carpentier GmbH opening a path to packaging business in Europe over the next few years, and Australia being prepared as a further market, with the first ROW packaging order (from a customer in South Africa) scheduled for delivery in the second quarter of FY27. On the technology side, the Company has built the whole ecosystem around RecTech — a dedicated nine-layer co-extrusion line coupled with compatible packaging and converting lines — launched at Plastindia 2026, and is moving into secondary packaging automation, which carries it further along the value chain and into much larger end markets. No rupee capex programme, capacity figure or commissioning schedule for a new plant is disclosed in the sections provided.
currentContext.mdna: FY26 results came in below the prior year, traced almost entirely to the United States — the largest export market — shrinking by close to half as prolonged tariff policy uncertainty led American clients to hold back from new CAPEX commitments|Two further pressures: the conflict in West Asia unsettled another set of buyers, and a steep rise in polymer prices strained customers' working capital across markets, prompting some to defer CAPEX plans|Demand beyond the United States stayed firm; India and other international markets each ended the year larger than before, with domestic packaging sales growing by 55%|Management expects margin pressure from a leaner export mix and some non-recurring costs to lift as volumes return, with profitability moving back toward its normal range in the year ahead|The company enters FY27 with better visibility than the previous year, and reads the backlog as a sign that underlying demand is strong|Growth in the coming year is expected to be led by packaging and supported by recovery across the other lines|Packaging is described as addressing the broadest opportunity set worldwide and holding the most room to compound|A recent government notification on recycled content adds to the case for adoption of recyclable technology among consumer brands; adoption is expected to be gradual as brands take a few quarters to qualify the format and volumes follow only once early adopters commit|By the end of the decade management expects Mamata to be led by packaging, far less reliant on any single country, with recyclable-ready technology contributing in earnest and profitability restored as greater scale and a richer export mix do their work|Innovation and the ability to integrate expertise across extrusion, converting and packaging technologies is cited as the continuing differentiator in the marketplace|Risks monitored include market conditions, customer demand, supply chain dynamics, regulatory developments, foreign exchange fluctuations, technological changes and other macroeconomic factors|Order book closed the year at ₹ 89.6 crore, 34% higher YOY — described as a backlog whose strength indicates underlying demand is strong, in a business where deliveries are uneven and best measured over a full year|First ROW packaging order booked during the year, from a customer in South Africa, scheduled for delivery in the second quarter of FY27, validating the packaging portfolio beyond the traditional US and Indian markets|Multi-machine order for vertical form-fill-seal (VFFS) lines from one of India's best-known snack and namkeen brands

one-line thesis: FY26 was a one-off "consolidation" year — a ~50% collapse in the high-margin US business (tariffs + West Asia + polymer inflation) crushed reported revenue (-8%) and EBITDA margin (21.4%→8.2%), but domestic packaging (+55%) and order book (+34% to Rs 89.6 cr) remained intact; management guides ~15% topline growth and margin normalization to ~20% in FY27.
financial scorecard: Revenue (FY26): Rs 233.1 cr vs Rs 254.6 cr FY25, -8% YoY. Q4FY26: Rs 73.9 cr vs Rs 111 cr Q4FY25 (~-33%). Driver: US business down ~50% in absolute terms (US = United States + Canada + Mexico).
EBITDA (FY26): Rs 19.1 cr @ 8.2% margin vs Rs 54.64 cr @ 21.4% FY25.
PAT (FY26, reported): Rs 15.1 cr vs Rs 40.8 cr FY25.
Gross margin: 54.6% FY26 vs 60.8% FY25 (-6.2pp). Export GM ~60% vs domestic GM ~42-43%.

Margin bridge (one-offs, mgmt explicit): gross-margin compression -6.2pp on EBITDA (lower export mix + adverse product mix [less co-extrusion] + commodity inflation absorbed in H2); one-time labour/wage-code provisioning Rs 3.05 cr booked entirely in Q4 = -1.3pp (new wage code effective 21-Nov-2025); elevated exhibition spend Rs 10.2 cr vs Rs 6.2 cr (lumpy, marquee shows clubbed in FY26) = -2.1pp; negative operating leverage on flat cost base.
Order book: Rs 89.59 cr (end-FY26) vs Rs 66.64 cr FY25, +34% YoY.
Cash / debt: Debt-free; cash on hand Rs 69.26 cr ("war chest").
Normalized read: mgmt expects profitability to normalize to ~20% EBITDA historical average as topline recovers and one-offs roll off.
guidance (critical): Revenue growth FY27: "conservatively ~15% higher topline" vs FY26 (off the lower base; declined to commit to the 18-20% consolidated target due to base).
Margin: normalize toward historical ~20% EBITDA as topline recovers and one-offs (wage-code provision, exhibition spend) roll off.

Segment guidance: domestic packaging 30-40% growth in FY27 (driven by FMCG new projects/capacity expansion, current pipeline — RecTech is incremental on top, NOT in this number); domestic converting double-digit growth; US to "make a comeback" / recoup lost ground.
Order book execution: of Rs 89.6 cr, ~Rs 80 cr is H1FY27; one Rs 9 cr 9-layer co-extrusion order is H2FY27. Mix: 62% exports / 38% domestic.

New geographies: SE Asia target ~US$1m initial; Europe incremental US$2-3m over 3-5 yrs (TAM ~US$800m for relevant product lines); Africa (South Africa) revenue starting; CIS/Russia & Australia in progress.
order book & pipeline (export vs domesti: Order book Rs 89.59 cr, +34% YoY; 62% export / 38% domestic.
~Rs 80 cr executes H1FY27; Rs 9 cr (9-layer co-extrusion) in H2FY27.
VFFS multi-machine order from a leading India snacks/namkeen brand: 4 machines delivered FY26 (3 in India), 18 more scheduled H1FY27 — gives strong FY27 visibility.
First-ever packaging order outside US/India: from South Africa, delivery Q2FY27.
Three machines (~Rs 3.5 cr) ready on shop floor for Saudi Arabia, shipment stuck due to West Asia crisis (delayed, not cancelled).
segment / subsidiary detail (fy26 vs fy2: Converting machinery: US fell from Rs 31.63 cr → Rs 5.93 cr (-81%, machines only); domestic converting +~6% (+Rs 3 cr); rest-of-world converting +23% (+Rs 11.5 cr). Present in ~84-86 countries; top-5 global brand by recall; highly fragmented market.
Packaging machinery (~Rs 48-49 cr FY26): US Rs 29.4 cr vs Rs 36.8 cr (-20%); domestic packaging +55%. Overall packaging flat (-1%).
Co-extrusion blown film: marginal degrowth (lumpiness, not momentum loss); 3 large 9-layer orders this year — 2 delivered FY26, 1 pending H2FY27; tightly linked to RecTech.
US-business recovery offset math: US drop ~Rs 31 cr in FY26; Rs 20.65 cr recovered (domestic converting +Rs 3 cr, domestic packaging +Rs 6 cr, RoW converting +Rs 11.5 cr) → net 8% topline decline.
Customer mix: converting & extrusion customers are B2B; packaging-machinery customers are FMCG (end-market B2C).
growth verticals / optionality: RecTech — fully recyclable mono-material film tech (launched at Blast India 2026); outperforms PET+PE / METPET+PE; bridges cost gap with high-priced recyclable films; tailwind from 31-Mar-2026 Govt gazette notification on recycled-PET/EPR mandate. Trials underway with a couple of large FMCGs; certified by Indian Institute of Packaging (barrier) and CIPET (recyclability); pursuing EU/US Class-A certification. Adoption 12-18 months before traction; incremental to the 30-40% packaging guide.
EU patent (Jan 2026) for "cross-sealing device" (already patented in India & US) — embedded in machines, being offered to European customers post-Interpack.

Europe entry via Carpentier GmbH (40-yr-old German end-of-line player); machines moved to their factory for demos; non-exclusive W. Europe; secondary HFFS solution co-developed; Eastern Europe via additional partners later. TAM ~US$800m.
New geographies: Africa (South Africa live), CIS/Russia (board-approved branch office; 100-yr-old local distributor), SE Asia (channel partners, ~US$1m target), Australia, CIS.
margins & cost dynamics: Export GM ~60% vs domestic ~42-43% — so US collapse mechanically dented blended GM (lower export share is the single largest factor, -6.2pp on EBITDA).
Costs are largely semi-variable/constant → disproportionate operating de-leverage on the way down (and re-leverage on the way up: cited ~10% topline growth FY25 → ~18% PAT growth).
Input-cost inflation (polymer/crude) "majority passed on" to customers; capital-goods custom builds priced project-by-project.
capex / expansion: No new-plant capex announced this call; focus is geographic/channel expansion (Germany partner, Russia branch office) and R&D (RecTech, cross-sealing, secondary HFFS) — funded internally from Rs 69.26 cr cash, debt-free.
Watch: capacity/commissioning not flagged as a constraint; execution risk sits more in order timing than plant build-out.
capital allocation: Debt-free; Rs 69.26 cr cash retained as risk-mitigation "war chest" for expansion/tech investment without borrowing.
R&D funded internally; dividend vs R&D balance addressed only loosely (no specific payout commitment given on call).
risks & watch-items: US tariff exposure (US is largest, highest-margin export market; US+Canada+Mexico bloc fell ~50%) — recovery is the key FY27 swing factor; residual headwinds from West Asia on customer sentiment/capex.
West Asia conflict — directly delayed Rs 3.5 cr Saudi shipment; broader macro/sentiment drag.
Lumpy machine orders (esp. co-extrusion 9-layer; exhibition-spend lumpiness).
Polymer/crude price volatility stretching customer working capital → deferred capex.
RecTech adoption slow (12-18 month qualification); Europe is "long game," Indian-brand perception hurdle.
Base-effect / guidance conservatism (15% off a depressed base ≈ still below prior run-rate).
management quality / tone: Unusually candid and detailed: CEO front-loaded a structured margin bridge and quantified each one-off; gave segment-level absolute revenue splits on request. Tone confident but measured (explicitly "conservative" on Europe and FY27 growth; cautioned not to over-extrapolate RecTech). Credible, numbers-forward IR.
non-obvious takeaways: The "8% revenue decline" masks an ~81% collapse in US converting machines and a Rs 31 cr US hole that was ~2/3 backfilled — underlying domestic engine (packaging +55%, converting +6%, RoW +23%) is healthy.
Reported PAT Rs 15.1 cr embeds ~Rs 3.05 cr wage-code one-off + ~Rs 4 cr incremental exhibition spend; normalized earnings power materially higher.
Regulatory tailwind: 31-Mar-2026 recycled-PET/EPR gazette notification is a structural demand pull for RecTech + 9-layer co-extrusion (the two are linked).
"US" = NAFTA bloc (US+Canada+Mexico), so the tariff shock had a wider footprint than the label suggests.
Pricing power is real: claims to be the most expensive supplier in India, winning on cost-to-output ratio, USFDA/3A dairy hygiene standard, and embedded patented cross-sealing for recyclable films.
qoq change log: Q4 FY26 (this): First full-year/Q4 framing as a "consolidation year." US business -~50% (converting machines -81%) on tariffs + West Asia + polymer inflation → revenue -8% (Rs 233.1 cr), EBITDA margin 21.4%→8.2%, PAT Rs 15.1 cr. Quantified one-offs: Rs 3.05 cr wage-code provision (-1.3pp), ~Rs 4 cr incremental exhibition (-2.1pp), GM -6.2pp. Order book +34% to Rs 89.6 cr (62/38 export/domestic). FY27 guide: ~15% topline, ~20% EBITDA normalization, domestic packaging 30-40%. New: RecTech launch + EU cross-sealing patent, Carpentier GmbH (Germany/Europe), South Africa first order, Russia/CIS branch office, SE Asia channel. Debt-free, cash Rs 69.26 cr.
